test_title: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 04 Sept, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: On May 20, 2025, the Supreme Court reinstated which requirement for candidates aspiring to become civil judges (junior division)?

options.text: Three years of legal practice experience
Passing a national-level judicial service exam

solution:
The correct answer is __**Three years of legal practice experience**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Supreme Court on May 20, 2025, reinstated the requirement of **three years of legal practice experience** for candidates aspiring to become civil judges (junior division).
 
• This decision was made to ensure that candidates possess adequate practical legal knowledge and understanding before serving as judicial officers.
 
• The requirement was previously in place but had been removed in several states, leading to debates about the readiness of fresh law graduates for judicial roles.
 
• The ruling aligns with the need to enhance the quality of judicial services by incorporating practical exposure into the eligibility criteria for civil judges.
 
• States and union territories will now need to implement this requirement in their judicial service examinations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Supreme Court (Composition & Appointment):**

 
 
• Judges: Chief Justice of India (CJI) + up to 33 other Judges (total 34).
 
• Appointment: Appointed by the President, with significant consultation from the Collegium (CJI & senior judges).
 
• Tenure: Judges retire at 65 years of age.
 
• Removal: Only by Parliament through a rigorous impeachment process for proven misbehavior or incapacity.
